  COVID- 19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

  Due to the existing COVID - 19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be allowed only to observe and address the City Council Meeting of December 7, 2021, at 2:00 p.m. (Or 1:00 p.m. if Closed Session) by telephone, video and other electronic means, as follows:

Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, City Clerk staff will check and print emails prior to arriving in the Council Chambers. In the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310 - 412- 5280 with any questions.

Inglewood, California
  December 7, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
December 7, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Morales, Faulk;
  and;
  Absent:  Council Member Padilla.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/ Public Works
  Director

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman
  Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager/Acting Executive Director*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager/CFO *
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas, other than the public hearings.
Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item No. 2,
Approval of the minutes of the meeting held on November 9, 2021 (Special).

Ray Howler, District 4 resident, spoke concerning PH-1, PH-2, and PH-3. He was
advised to call back during the Public Hearing portion.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/

  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated

  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – RESOLUTION NO. 22-19 ADOPTED –
  CERTIFYING AN ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT, ADOPTING A
  STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS, AND ADOPTING A
  MITIGATION  MONITORING  AND  REPORTING  PROGRAM  IN
  ACCORDANCE WITH CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT
  FOR THE WESTCHESTER/VETERANS AND CRENSHAW/IMPERIAL
  TRANSIT ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT PLAN; RESOLUTION NO. 22-20
  ADOPTED – AMENDMENTS TO THE LAND USE ELEMENT OF THE
  INGLEWOOOD COMPREHENSIVE GENERAL PLAN (GPA-2021-01) TO
  INCLUDE GOALS AND POLICIES FOR THE WESTCHESTER/VETERANS
  AND CRENSHAW/IMPERIAL TRANSIT ORIENTED DISTRICT LAND USE
  DESIGNATIONS; ORDINANCE NO. 22-02 INTRODUCED – APPROVING
  ZONE CHANGE ZC-2021-001 TO ESTABLISH TRANSIT ORIENTED ZONES;
  ORDINANCE NO. 22-03 INTRODUCED – APPROVING ZONE CODE
  AMENDMENT ZCA-2021-004 TO CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE; RESOLUTION NO. 22-21 ADOPTED – ADOPTION OF
  THE WESTCHESTER/VETERANS AND CRENSHAW/IMPERIAL TRANSIT
  ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT PLAN AND DESIGN GUIDELINES. The City
  Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider multiple
  actions associated with the Westchester/Veterans and Crenshaw/Imperial Transit
  Oriented Development Plan and Design Guidelines, notice had been given in the time,
  form and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and communications were
  received, and distributed to the City Council.

  Louis Atwell, Acting City Manager presented the staff report dated December 7, 2021.

  Christopher E. Jackson Sr., Economic and Community Development Department
  Director gave an oral report to provide clarity on the intent and purpose of the two Transit
  Oriented Development (TOD) Plans, Westchester/Veterans and Crenshaw/Imperial. He
  reported that the Westchester/Veterans and Crenshaw/Imperial areas have transit stations
  around them and for that reason, the City received a grant from Metro that allowed transit
  stops in Inglewood. He also reported the TOD Plan and Design Guidelines presented an
  opportunity to consider and evaluate what type of zoning was appropriate for those
  designated areas. It also presented an opportunity to consider how the city could align the
  Metro stations with the growth of the city, in addition to the impact it would have on

  2
 December 7, 2021

  general and affordable housing. He stated during the Planning and Commission hearing,
  the residents raised concerns, which resulted in modifications to the TOD Plan. He also
  stated the Draft TOD Plans were endorsed by the Planning Commission and
  recommended the following actions: Certification of the Final Environmental Impact
  Report; Adoption of General Plan Amendment; Adoption of Zoning Code Amendment
  associated with this project; and then adoption of Westchester/Veterans and
  Crenshaw./Imperial Transit Oriented Design Plans and Guidelines. Finally, he provided
  clarity to the residents by answering some frequently asked questions.

  Mayor Butts left the dais at the hour of 2:15 p.m.

  Mayor Butts returned to the dais at the hour of 2:16 p.m.

  Mindy Wilcox, AICP Planning Manager, gave an oral report on the stakeholder meetings,
  community workshops, pop-up events, and pop-up outreach plan events that were located
  in the TOD Plan areas. As part of the plans, she described the land usage for
  Westchester/Veterans and Crenshaw/ Imperial TOD plans, which included new zoning
  designations and regulations. She also reported that some of the TOD Plans modified
  building height, building setbacks, parking regulations, the planning approval process
  required, and form based requirements among others. She reviewed the five actions
  requested from the Council, which is listed in the staff report. Finally, she reported that
  Phil Burns, a representative from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Consulting Group was on the phone to answer questions.

  Following a brief discussion with Mindy Wilcox, AICP Planning Manager, Mayor Butts
  inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City Council on the
  Public Hearing.

  Chris (Last Name Unknown) Advocate for a 91-year-old senior veteran, opposed the
  Crenshaw/Imperial Transit Oriented Design Project. She stated her belief is that air
  pollution and the noise wasn’t factored into the project. She also stated she was annoyed
  by the street takeovers that took place on Crenshaw and Imperial.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke concerning the stakeholders being informed and the
  outreach to the constituents. She suggested that the city provide information to residents
  at their homes or mailing addresses. She also spoke on the naming of the Fairview
  Heights Apartments, naming it one of the oldest sections of Inglewood. Lastly, she
  recommended that the city should consider improvements on the streets and sidewalks.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke concerning a letter from the Economic and Community
  Development Department regarding the parking requirements for all developed areas that
  are proposed to be reduced from the current requirements. He stated if the Council took a
  visit, they would discover on the east side of Crenshaw, one block north of the Metro
  Station that residents from the multi-story apartment complex consumed majority of the
  street parking, and the TOD Plan was counterproductive to the city’s residential parking
  permit program. Finally, he requested that the parking requirements in the Transit
  Oriented Development Plant not be reduced.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke on the overlay connected to the Green-Line Crenshaw
  Station, and stated the city has dealt with this since February, 2015. Additionally, he
  discussed the community meetings that were held and felt that the TOD Plan should be
  discussed further.

  Mayor Butts closed public comments at the hour of 2:41 p.m.

  Following discussion it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 22-19 entitled:

  3
 December 7, 2021

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  CALIFORNIA, CERTIFYING AN ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT,
  ADOPTING ENVIRONMENTAL FINDINGS ADOPTING A STATEMENT OF
  OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS AND ADOPTING A MITIGATION
  MONITORING AND REPORTING PROGRAM IN ACCORDANCE WITH
  THE CALIFORNIA ENVIORNMENTAL QUALITY ACT FOR THE
  WESTCHESTER/VETERANS AND CRENSHAW/IMPERIAL TRANSIT
  ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT PLAN

  and; 2) Adopt Resolution No. 22-20 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPTING AMENDMENTS
  TO THE LAND USE ELEMENT OF THE INGLEWOOD
  COMPREHENSIVE GENERAL PLAN (GPA-2021-01) TO INCLUDE
  GOALS AND POLICIES FOR THE WESTCHESTER/VETERANS AND
  CRENSHAW/IMPERIAL TRANSIT ORIENTED DISTRICT LAND USE
  DESIGNATIONS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 22-02 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING ZONE CHANGE ZC-2021-
  001 TO ESTABLISH TRANSIT ORIENTED ZONES

  was introduced by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 22-03 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD.,  CALIFORNIA,  APPROVING  ZONING  CODE
  AMENDMENT ZCA 2021-004 TO CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE (IMC)

  was introduced by Council Member Morales; and 3) Adopt Resolution No. 22-21
  entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,  ADOPTING  THE
  WESTCHESTER/VETERANS  CRENSHAW/IMPERIAL  TRANSIT
  ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT PLAN AND DESIGN GUIDELINES

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and

  4
   December 7, 2021

  Noes: None.

142  PUBLIC HEARING HELD - RESOLUTION NO. 22-22 ADOPTED – AMENDING
  THE MASTER FEE SCHEDULE BY ADDING TRANSPORTATION IMPACT
  FEES. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to
  receive public comments on the consideration to adopt a resolution amending the Master
  Fee Schedule by adding Transportation Impact Fees, notice had been given in the time,
  form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and communications have
  been received and distributed to Council.

  Louis Atwell, Acting City Manager presented the staff report dated December 7, 2021.

  Sharon Kioke, Assistant Finance Director presented a brief oral report on the overview of
  the Transportation Impact Fees, and why the City of Inglewood was interested in
  implementing them.

  Following a brief discussion with Sharon Kioke, Assistant Finance Director, Mayor Butts
  inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City Council on the
  Public Hearing.

  Council Member Dotson left the dais at the hour of 2:55 p.m.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke regarding the Clippers Area, and wanted to know the
  status of the project. She also spoke on SB 9 and SB 10, and felt that there was no single
  home residential zoning because of these legislative bills. Lastly, she stated the
  homeowners in the Fairview Heights area would have to redevelop their homes in
  addition to the maintenance.

  Mayor Butts closed public comment at the hour of 2:56 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that Resolution No. 22-22 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, ESTABLISHING A TRANSPORTATION IMPACT FEE (TIF)

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  Council Member Dotson returned to the dais at the hour of 2:57 p.m.

183  PUBLIC HEARING HELD - RESOLUTION NO. 22-23 ADOPTED – ADOPTING
  A NEW WATER CONNECTION AND CAPACITY FEE IN ACCORDANCE
  WITH AB 1600, AS CODIFIED BY CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE 66000,
  ET SEQ. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to
  receive public comments on the consideration to adopt a resolution establishing a new
  Water Capacity Charge (WCC) in accordance with AB 1600, as codified by California
  Government Code 66000, et. seq., notice had been given in the time, form and manner as
  required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no communications were received.

  Louis Atwell, Acting City Manager presented the staff report dated December 7, 2021.
  He also presented a brief overview of the Water Capacity Charge, stating this is similar to
  the Transportation Impact Fees, and it only applies to future infrastructures.

  Michael Whipple, in association with Steven Bucknam & Associates, Inc., presented a
  brief oral report.

  Council Member Morales left the dais at the hour of 3:01 p.m.

  5
   December 7, 2021

  Mayor Butts gave a brief overview of the New Water Connection and Capacity Fee.

  Council Member Morales returned to the dais at the hour of 3:03 p.m.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  There was no response.

  Mayor Butts closed public comments at the hour of 3:03 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member Faulk that Resolution No. 22-23 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA ADOPTING A NEW WATER
  CONNECTION AND CAPACITY FEE AND ORDERING THE
  PLACEMENT OF SAID FEE INTO THE CITY’S MASTER FEE
  SCHEDULE

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

131.8  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – DRAFT FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021
  CONSOLIDATED ANNUAL PERFORMANCE EVALUATION REPORT
  (CAPER) APPROVED. The City Clerk announced that the next scheduled matter was a
  public hearing to consider approval of the Draft Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Consolidated
  Annual Performance Evaluation Report (CAPER) for submission to the U.S. Department
  of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Los Angeles Field Office by December 30,
  2021, deadline, notice had been given in the time, form and manner as required by law,
  an affidavit was on file, and no communications were received.

  Louis Atwell, Acting City Manager presented the staff report dated December 7, 2021.

  Roberto Chavez, HUD Manager, presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on the Public Hearing.

  Caller (Name Unknown) expressed her concern regarding the HUD Report and requested
  that potential African-American homebuyers be treated fairly. She also spoke about
